Create realistic 16:9 stage footage. Keep the audience off camera and every featured face under soft neutral frontal light. Ice-blue lighting remains behind and beside the performers. Equally visible members share subtle non-phonetic mouth motion.
[Shot 1] Medium-close portrait of M1 in ZF-left, with M2, M3, and M4 softly separated in diagonal depth across ZC behind her. M1 starts with her right hand low, slices it diagonally upward across her body, reaches a clean impact point beside her shoulder, then lowers it toward M2's direction. The camera makes a very small portrait push; M1 keeps subtle non-phonetic mouth motion and confident eye contact. Her hand and face remain fully visible.
[Shot 2] At 00:03.200, hard cut to a medium-close portrait of M2 from a discontinuous right-front viewpoint. M2 receives the visual handoff: her left hand rises from waist level, folds into an open angular frame beside her cheek without covering it, then completes a downward wrist turn. M1, M3, and M4 remain readable in the deeper plane, sharing the same restrained mouth state. The camera stays steady and the right-side ice-blue line brightens.
[Shot 3] At 00:06.500, hard cut to an eye-level mid-thigh shot of all four. They begin in diagonal depth, take one coordinated side step, execute a synchronized lateral arm hit, and finish as a balanced ZC line in stable M1→M4 left-to-right identity order. A short lateral camera follow resolves to a fixed composition. Their feet settle, arms finish at their sides, faces remain separated, and the completed line holds through the end.
